title: SDK scrollable-batch & streaming-retry helpers for embeddings + rerank (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Ana Chen
description: Implement a consistent, ergonomic set of helpers across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to handle scrollable pagination and batching for embeddings and reranking endpoints, and a streaming-retry adapter for long-running rerank/stream calls. Goal is API parity, predictable cost/latency trade-offs, and easy examples for customers migrating from single-request loops to efficient batch/stream patterns.
proposed_solution: Publish a small, well-named utilities package in each SDK: "ScrollableBatch" iterator for cursor/offset-less scrolling, "Batcher" helpers for adaptive batching by token/record limits, and "StreamRetryAdapter" to apply idempotent-aware retry/backoff logic to streaming rerank endpoints. Expose simple sync/async patterns in Python, Promises/async iterators in TS, and channels/iterators in Go. Provide clear opt-in defaults for concurrency, max in-flight requests, and memory caps. Implement tests and end-to-end examples showing embeddings vectorization then rerank flow.
implementation_notes:
- Python: async generator + sync wrapper. Use client.fetch_embeddings_batch() + client.rerank_stream() examples. Backoff config using tenacity for retries (configurable).
- TypeScript: AsyncIterable helper and takeWhile style windowing; expose setBatchLimits({records, tokens}).
- Go: channel-based iterator with context cancellation and bounded worker pool.
- All SDKs: surface telemetry hooks (timing, tokens per batch) and opt-out hooks for advanced users.
- Benchmarks: microbenchmarks for median latency and cost per 1k items across common batch sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs each provide ScrollableBatch and StreamRetryAdapter APIs with equivalent names and semantic behavior
End-to-end example: take 10k short documents, create embeddings in ~200-500 sized batches, then perform streaming rerank with checkpointing and automatic retries; included in repo examples
Unit + integration tests covering backoff, idempotency detection, partial-stream resume behavior, and concurrency limits
Docs: API reference, migration guide (from naive loops), code snippets for sync/async patterns, and recommended batch profiles for typical workloads
Performance: documented latency and token-cost guidance for three recommended batch profiles (small/medium/large) based on microbenchmarks
Telemetry: SDK emits batch size and tokens-per-request metrics to Redwood telemetry by default (opt-out flag documented)
Release gated by demo with Solutions + a short internal training session and sign-off from DX and Runtime owners
